rationale: class_prevalence gives positive/negative counts, prevalence and imbalance ratio with fraud_prevalence.png. leakage_assessment is switched on because the task explicitly requires a named assessment of label-derived, identifier and protected fields. feature_comparison is restricted to claim-level fields that are legitimately available and not label-derived: fraud_pattern_type is excluded as label-derived (non-null on only 647 of 12845 rows, i.e. essentially the flagged set); member_sex, member_race_ethnicity and member_age_band are excluded as protected attributes; member_payer_type is excluded as a member-level attribute and a plausible proxy for age/income, keeping the comparison claim-level and avoiding the join entirely. The 13 retained features cover coding (claim_type, cpt_category, place_of_service), provider context (provider_specialty, network_status), financials (billed/allowed/paid), utilisation (service_units, length_of_stay) and operational flags (er_flag, auth_required_flag, high_cost_flag). Report prints every rate as numerator/denominator, cites artifacts for each result, and states synthetic data, descriptive-only, association-not-causation, small groups (flagged group is ~5% so categorical cells can be thin), class imbalance and no operational use. No skills were provided for this step.
